singlePurpose: Capture, protect, review, and export meeting transcripts. Better CaptionKeep reads displayed captions from supported Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, and Zoom Web pages and lets a signed-in organizational user select a recent Teams meeting and privately import its authorized official transcript from Microsoft 365 when their tenant permits the delegated access. Transcript data stays in the user's browser unless the user explicitly exports or copies it.

permissionJustifications.downloads: Used to save user-requested or user-configured transcript exports as TXT or Markdown files and to open the browser's default downloads folder when requested. The permission is not used to download remote content.
permissionJustifications.activeTab: Used when the user opens the extension popup to identify the active supported meeting tab and communicate with the extension's caption-capture content script. Access is limited to the user-invoked active-tab workflow.
permissionJustifications.storage: Used for extension preferences, capture-recovery checkpoints, pending exports, temporary speaker aliases, and the user-controlled local transcript archive. Managed enterprise settings are also read through the browser's managed-storage system. The developer does not operate a transcript-storage service.
permissionJustifications.unlimitedStorage: Allows the local transcript archive to retain more than chrome.storage.local's default 10 MB quota without silently evicting older meetings. Archive data remains on this browser profile until the user deletes it, the extension is removed, or an explicit managed retention policy applies.
permissionJustifications.sidePanel: Used to display the live transcript, recovery status, speaker tools, search, Scrubby privacy controls, and export actions alongside the supported meeting page. The side panel is opened only as part of the user's local caption-capture workflow and does not transmit transcript data to a developer-operated service.
permissionJustifications.identity: Used when the user chooses Connect Microsoft 365. It opens an interactive multi-tenant Microsoft Entra authorization-code flow with PKCE so an organizational user can find recent Teams meetings and explicitly import an authorized official transcript when their tenant permits the delegated scopes. Tokens stay in browser session storage, and no client secret is embedded in the extension.

oauthScopeJustifications.openid: Confirms the identity returned by Microsoft during the interactive organizational sign-in flow.
oauthScopeJustifications.profile: Displays the connected Microsoft 365 account label so the user can verify which organizational account is active.
oauthScopeJustifications.offline_access: Allows Microsoft to refresh the delegated session while the browser remains open without repeatedly interrupting the user. The refresh token stays only in browser session storage.
oauthScopeJustifications.Calendars.ReadBasic: Reads only basic event fields needed to show up to five recent Teams meetings: subject, start and end time, organizer flag, and Teams join information. Calendar results are not written to transcript history or browser sync.
oauthScopeJustifications.OnlineMeetings.Read: Resolves the one Teams meeting the user selected by its join link or meeting ID before requesting its transcript.
oauthScopeJustifications.OnlineMeetingTranscript.Read.All: Lists and retrieves an official transcript only after the signed-in user explicitly chooses an authorized Teams meeting. Microsoft and tenant policy determine which transcripts the user can access.

hostPermissionJustification: Required meeting-origin access is limited to Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, and Zoom Web for local caption capture. Microsoft identity and Graph origins are optional and requested only after the user selects Connect Microsoft 365; they support interactive sign-in, up to five recent eligible Teams meetings, and retrieval of the one authorized official transcript the user selects. Calendar results remain transient. Better CaptionKeep does not access unrelated websites, record audio or video, or send transcripts to a developer-operated service.
